nodes.description: Immutable IERC20 liquidity asset token address that the Loan was funded with, held in custody by FundingLocker.
Immutable address of the Loan contract authorized to pull or drain the escrowed liquidity asset.
Constructor that assigns the liquidity asset token and the owning Loan address.
Access-control modifier requiring msg.sender to equal the stored loan address before execution.
External isLoan-guarded function that transfers a caller-specified amount of liquidity asset to a destination address.
External isLoan-guarded function that transfers the entire liquidity asset balance held by this contract to the loan.
Caller-controlled address used as the authorization check value inside the isLoan modifier.
SafeERC20.safeTransfer external token call in pull(), performing a low-level call to the token with attacker-influenced dst and amt.
SafeERC20.safeTransfer external token call in drain(), transferring the full balance to the loan address.
External liquidityAsset.balanceOf(address(this)) call in drain() used to compute the amount to transfer.
Constructor parameter address _liquidityAsset, the ERC20 token to be held.
Constructor parameter address _loan, the Loan contract allowed to withdraw funds.
pull() parameter dst, the destination address for the transfer.
pull() parameter amt, the amount of liquidity asset to transfer.
Local variable amt in drain() holding the contract's full liquidity asset balance.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter _liquidityAsset is consumed by the constructor body.
Constructor parameter _loan is consumed by the constructor body.
_liquidityAsset is written into the immutable liquidityAsset state variable.
_loan is written into the immutable loan state variable.
msg.sender flows into the isLoan modifier authorization comparison.
Stored loan address is the trusted counterpart compared against msg.sender in isLoan.
isLoan modifier gates execution of pull().
isLoan modifier gates execution of drain().
pull() parameter dst is used within the function body.
pull() parameter amt is used within the function body.
pull() executes the safeTransfer unsafe operation.
liquidityAsset state variable is the token on which safeTransfer is invoked in pull().
Untrusted dst parameter flows into the token transfer recipient.
Untrusted amt parameter flows into the transferred token amount.
The external token call in pull() hands control to the token contract, which could re-enter pull before state settles.
drain() performs the balanceOf external call.
drain() performs the remaining-balance safeTransfer.
liquidityAsset is the token queried by balanceOf in drain().
Result of balanceOf is stored in the local variable amt.
Local amt is passed as the transfer amount into safeTransfer in drain().
liquidityAsset is the token on which safeTransfer is invoked in drain().
Stored loan address is used as the transfer recipient in drain().
External token transfer in drain() transfers control to the token contract, enabling re-entrant calls before completion.

Untrusted dst parameter is consumed directly as the transfer recipient of the safeTransfer operation in pull().
Untrusted amt parameter is consumed directly as the transfer amount of the safeTransfer operation in pull().
Local amt exists only to carry the balanceOf result into the safeTransfer amount in drain().
